batch_strategy: Use matched condition contrasts to repair endpoint-specific loading responses, resolve m182 completion behavior, and test selected solvent-response extrema. Add weak-eluent anchors where response transfer remains poorly established, especially m103 and m24.

choices.reason: m182 at 50/1 and 135 mg tests whether the positive completion-loading gap measured at 20/1 in db26f51c86dc787ac633 and 204c95299f49a2bcdb61 persists, collapses, or reverses. Predicted V2 is 36.44 mL, below the measured 45 mg 50/1 completion in 486e498e45d084ced568.

The 90 mg m182 50/1 point joins the selected 135 mg point and measured 45 mg record 486e498e45d084ced568. Predictions give almost identical completion at 90 and 135 mg, whereas d6f36b5de45565d68603 showed nonlinear amount interpolation at 1/1. This distinguishes interpolation shape from a uniform completion offset.

m208 in pure EA at 92.865 mg establishes a missing baseline. Predicted completion is 16.43 mL, suggesting a decrease toward the early 1/1 region. Pairing this with the selected higher amount tests whether the large onset amount association measured at 20/1 begins from a much smaller baseline difference.

m208 in pure EA at 278.595 mg directly precedes same-loading 1/1 observation 3fe8b9db9fbe9d0dedc4. The prediction implies completion falling from 16.54 to that measured 9.43 mL. This matched solvent comparison and the selected lower-amount baseline test a substantial predicted endpoint extremum.

m208 at 5/1 and 92.865 mg complements higher-amount observation bc62be727bf6ded3d86e. The prediction places lower-amount onset below the measured higher-amount onset, opposite the pronounced ordering at 20/1 in 5a7a5139767fda9f7e9a and b66aa101a244885dd587. This locates where the association develops.

m209 in pure EA at 68.75 mg starts a matched baseline loading pair. The measured 20/1 extremes, 1b4be0410f927930d56e and 29b39881584c4fec1c58, differ by 12.49 mL in onset but much less in completion. This tests whether that weak-eluent association is absent or reduced at the baseline.

The 206.25 mg m209 pure-EA point completes the baseline contrast. Predicted completion near 13.44 mL exceeds predictions near 9 mL at 1/1 and measured middle-amount 1/1 completion in cbf66c429d0d825609d6. Together with m208, this tests whether the proposed early completion decrease transfers between phenol environments.

m162 at 10/1 and 50 mg complements c82c1933ed710ffb4981 at 100 mg. Predicted lower-amount onset is 10.55 mL, below the measured middle-amount 12.31 mL, while the measured 50/1 ordering in 96e2b82e29c0b5205628 and 7b8eaa0c9205349f60b1 is reversed. This tests ratio-dependent loading response in an aryl nitrile.

m162 at 50/1 and 150 mg completes an amount series with 96e2b82e29c0b5205628 and 7b8eaa0c9205349f60b1. Its predicted onset of 20.63 mL exceeds the measured middle-amount onset despite the decrease from 50 to 100 mg. The label discriminates continued decrease, saturation, and reversal.

m163 at 10/1 and 55.8 mg complements middle-amount observation b4e38c1386009c8311ab. Predicted onset is below that measured middle-amount value, whereas fe212637596386c24049 and 4e417c41d918e49abba1 show the opposite ordering at 50/1. Comparison with the selected m162 point tests transfer across halogen environments.

m163 at 50/1 and 167.4 mg extends the measured 55.8 and 111.6 mg series in fe212637596386c24049 and 4e417c41d918e49abba1. Predictions flatten onset and reduce completion at the upper amount. Measuring this alongside m162 tests whether those responses are scaffold-specific or shared by these donor-free nitriles.

m67 at 5/1 and 49.7 mg begins a matched contrast before the large onset differences measured at 10/1 and 20/1. Current predictions are nearly amount-invariant at 5/1. This lower-amount point helps locate the solvent region where loading sensitivity appears in a secondary benzylic alcohol.

The matched 149.1 mg m67 5/1 experiment completes the contrast. db5dcc7b864e0174fcbd and 5e784130c58b8175024e showed a 5.88 mL onset difference at 10/1 with similar completion; the 20/1 difference was larger. The pair tests whether onset and completion diverge already at this earlier ratio.

m67 at 20/1 and 99.4 mg interpolates between 2cf4f6424b85ab121943 and 80f6a235bb59c2a7ea59, measured at 42.23/62.09 and 30.59/62.98 mL. The recent higher-amount onset miss was 10.36 mL at acquisition. This middle point tests smooth amount dependence versus an exceptional endpoint record.

m51 at 1/1 and 48.3 mg fills the solvent gap between measured pure-EA baseline 99cecaf5e0ea91ad4781 and 2/1 record a1ea7a9303a5fc7a7b0f. With the selected higher amount, it tests how the onset amount gap grows from 1.31 mL in pure EA to 3.06 mL at 2/1.

The 144.9 mg m51 1/1 point completes a local loading contrast. Predictions differ by only about 0.12 mL in onset across the selected amounts, despite the nonzero baseline gap in 99cecaf5e0ea91ad4781 and f91e857aa14399ede600 and the larger 2/1 gap. This supplies a direct test of early response interpolation.

m114 at 10/1 and 150 mg completes the series containing cde49c2f3cf630c3a2a2 and 5fb70d195002f8a4d518. Predicted onset rises above the measured 100 mg onset, whereas its measured 50/1 series decreases with amount. This tests whether the intermediate-eluent response saturates or genuinely reverses.

m110 at 50/1 and 168.9 mg extends d3047299bd8817ee87dd and ce39d1762993bbbafaca. Those lower amounts had decreasing onset but nearly identical completion around 36.1 mL. The new prediction lowers completion to 32.47 mL, testing whether the model couples both endpoints too strongly to amount.

m116 at 50/1 and 105.1 mg fills the interval between 7bfad75485e830b6d460 and 22300151ccec3f1f1c24. Predicted completion, 49.99 mL, is below both measured extremes, while onset interpolates between them. This tests an unsupported completion trough and separates the two endpoint responses.

m125 in pure EA at 150 mg and 300 uL DCM tests the predicted upper-amount rise to 7.06/17.74 mL. At 100 mg, e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2 and dd4f07e349873053fd73 show very different baselines for 300 versus 500 uL DCM. This label constrains amount extrapolation within the 300 uL context.

m69 at 10/1 and 97.5 mg supplies an interior anchor before a1089c52394c961fdb05 at 20/1 and 712efbedcb59418d3a25 at 50/1. The latter onset rose to 9.69 mL, weakening flat-onset transfer from m68 and m70. This measurement locates the earlier response before that weak-eluent rise.

m68 at 5/1 and 102.2 mg connects e3716bf7dba67a0f2185 at 2/1 to f1e08c239f1c0950ad36 at 10/1. The new 10/1 label rejected the predicted onset dip and placed completion above the measured 20/1 completion. This point tests where completion curvature develops while onset stays relatively flat.

m70 at 50/1 and 47.3 mg complements b7bebdf1c141f2ae938e at 141.9 mg. The latter maintained early onset while completion increased. A lower-amount label tests whether that flat onset belongs to the molecular response generally or is partly associated with the higher recorded loading.

m103 at 20/1 and 101 mg begins a matched weak-eluent response pair following 53c040ff6322144b3053 at 10/1. Its 7.03/13.88 mL prediction suggests little completion growth initially. This uncovered segment tests response transfer among methyl benzoates; high CW distance is supplementary coverage evidence.

The matched m103 50/1 point predicts 12.27/18.08 mL, implying a later onset rise after the selected 20/1 point. Measured chloro analogue ede97e1f4b6e7fe9a7eb has a longer completion at 50/1 under its own recorded conditions. The pair tests whether the iodobenzoate response shape is learned appropriately.

m24 at 20/1 and 44 mg starts a matched pair in a sparsely measured hydrocarbon curve. Existing 10/1 record e9a472ec6320a7295dd0 is at 88 mg, so it does not establish this lower-amount response. The label tests whether the predicted late onset growth starts before 50/1.

m24 at 50/1 and 44 mg completes the pair, predicting onset rising from 6.52 to 9.78 mL. This is a stronger onset response than measured for several other donor-free aromatic hydrocarbons, including m14 in fc5fa646f4ee783c186a and 258fba623c2f3e812f54. The label tests structural response transfer beyond H-bond descriptors.

m174 at 20/1 and 54.85 mg begins an amount contrast before measured 30/1 records 704ba630f25fe7f20166 and 34cf0942ff52b1b80385. Those records associate higher amount with substantially later completion. This tests whether that association emerges already at 20/1 despite nearly invariant predictions.

The matched 164.55 mg m174 20/1 point completes the contrast. Predicted V2 differs from the lower amount by only about 0.11 mL, compared with an 8.71 mL measured difference at 30/1. Both labels distinguish a localized response from an amount relationship the model currently suppresses.

m11 at 20/1 and 50 mg extends the loading question to an oxime. Middle-amount observation 2f48e798c7917fb7d2ae measured 17.68/45.32 mL, but the extremes remain unmeasured. Together with the selected higher amount, this tests whether alcohol-like onset sensitivity transfers to the distinct N–OH environment.

m11 at 20/1 and 150 mg completes a matched loading panel around 2f48e798c7917fb7d2ae. Predictions are nearly invariant across amount, while 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f shows a much steeper later solvent response at 50/1. This tests endpoint-specific amount effects before that later rise.

m59 at 5/1 and 116.2 mg fills the gap between 036352f6818925e928f6 at 2/1 and recent fde9781e6b15ffbe093f at 10/1. Predicted onset falls slightly below the measured 2/1 onset before rising sharply at 10/1. This locates the response knee and tests another proposed onset dip.

hypotheses.content: Across several molecular environments, weaker eluent increases the association between recorded loading amount and onset, often with much smaller completion changes. Magnitude, direction, and saturation remain molecule- and ratio-dependent; a universal loading offset is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many remaining predictions are almost invariant across amount. Matched contrasts can teach structure-by-solvent-by-loading relationships and prevent onset and completion from inheriting the same response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the m67 and m51 onset gaps develop, and do nitriles, methoxy aromatics, and an oxime show continued decreases, saturation, or reversals across the selected amounts?

hypotheses.content: m182 requires a substantial completion baseline and solvent-dependent completion-loading response separate from its early onset. Recent measurements rejected the proposed completion decreases from 2/1 to 5/1 at 90 mg and from 10/1 to 20/1 at 135 mg. Whether the positive 20/1 completion-loading gap continues at 50/1 is unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Repeated acquisition-time misses were concentrated in completion. The selected upper and middle amounts test whether retraining has learned the endpoint-specific response or merely adjusted nearby baselines.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, does completion increase with amount as at 20/1, and how does the 90 mg point interpolate between 45 and 135 mg?

hypotheses.content: Early solvent-response extrema are scaffold- and endpoint-specific. The m7 peak and m10 completion decrease were measured, while the predicted m38 completion decrease and m68 onset dip were not supported. The phenol baseline decreases and m59 onset dip selected here remain untested instances.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct anchors can preserve genuine curvature while correcting interpolation artifacts. A shared monotonic response for both endpoints would conflict with supplied measurements.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted pure-EA completion baselines for m208 and m209 above their 1/1 region, and does m59 onset actually decrease between 2/1 and 5/1?

hypotheses.content: The earlier proposal that both m69 and m70 inherit m68's nearly flat weak-eluent onset is only partly supported. m70 remains consistent with that pattern at its measured higher amount, but m69 onset rises substantially from 20/1 to 50/1. Carbonyl environment and scaffold therefore limit response transfer within this ketone group.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These related ketones offer a focused test of which structural similarities justify transferring onset and completion curves. The m70 amount contrast also checks whether the apparent scaffold distinction depends on loading.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m69's onset rise begin, what completion curvature occurs around m68 5/1, and does m70 retain early onset at lower amount in 50/1 eluent?

hypotheses.content: The positive amount association in m174 completion measured at 30/1 may already emerge at 20/1. This would differ from the small completion changes seen in several other selected loading panels. The inference rests on a limited local contrast and remains tentative.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This pair tests a potentially different endpoint-loading relationship rather than extending only the common onset-dominated pattern. It can teach when completion also needs substantial amount sensitivity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched 20/1 conditions, does increasing amount from 54.85 to 164.55 mg appreciably increase completion, or is the 30/1 contrast localized?

hypotheses.content: m125 shows substantial associations with recorded loading-solvent volume in the early solvent region, but their size and endpoint pattern change with PE/EA. Its upper-amount pure-EA response at 300 uL DCM should therefore be learned within that context rather than inferred by pooling 500 uL records.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This tests an amount-by-loading-volume context that broad molecular descriptors cannot identify. The measurements establish catalog associations, without isolating a causal solvent-volume mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 150 mg pure-EA result at 300 uL DCM show the predicted completion rise above the measured lower amounts, or remain near their shorter baseline?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen solvent-dependent loading associations beyond the original alcohol and ester examples. m67 at 20/1 differed by 11.64 mL in onset between the measured extremes while completion differed by less than 1 mL; the higher-amount onset prediction missed by 10.36 mL at acquisition. The lower-amount m208, m209, m162, and m163 labels also revealed onset underpredictions and support testing where their amount responses emerge. The m51 pure-EA contrast was smaller than its weaker-eluent contrasts, but its 1.31 mL onset gap means the baseline should not be treated as exactly amount-invariant. For m182, the 90 mg 1/1 completion lay near the higher-amount value, and completion increased across both selected solvent extensions that had been predicted to decrease. This shifts the next repair toward its unresolved 50/1 amount response. The m7 onset peak was confirmed, so the previous concern about sparse-model extrema cannot become a universal rejection rule. Conversely, m38 completion increased from 1/1 to 2/1, and m68 did not show the predicted onset dip. m70 supported relatively flat onset at its measured amount, whereas m69's 50/1 onset weakened pooled flat-onset transfer. The new m201 points support its relatively flat-onset branch, reducing priority for further sampling based solely on its nitro group. These errors are historical acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals. Observed tuple assignments take precedence over historical reasons: m208's middle-amount 20/1 record is 0b8c6c59ae5e24b420e5; 0b8c7bc2949fb8070c94 belongs to m73.
batch_rationale: The 32 choices combine failure repair with discriminating local experiments and selected coverage extensions. The loading panels address a recurring model behavior—nearly invariant amount predictions despite measured endpoint-specific associations—and include tests of emergence, saturation, reversal, and completion sensitivity. Existing middle or extreme amounts make these labels informative without repeatedly measuring the same tuples. The two m182 labels target a recent completion-specific failure and distinguish a persistent loading gap from a weak-eluent plateau. Phenol baselines, m59's missing interior, and the focused ketone comparisons resolve response shape while retaining the possibility of genuine nonmonotonic behavior. The m125 point tests amount extrapolation within a loading-volume context with measured differences. Matched m103 and m24 solvent pairs explore less established weak-eluent responses in a benzoate and a hydrocarbon, helping the model learn when structural response transfer is justified. All selected molecule-plus-condition tuples are distinct, and duplicate candidate aliases are not jointly selected. Amount is density times recorded sample volume; these comparisons test supplied-condition associations, with missing experimental factors still unresolved. Quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and CW distance is only supplementary coverage evidence. Together, the labels should improve Row-distribution prediction by teaching interactions among structure, eluent strength, loading conditions, and the two endpoints separately.
